question: Can this one GT-free fixed-K20 protected insertion rule safely admit useful learned paths?
answer: No. Policy outputs exactly native20 for every evaluated row; safe fallback, zero complement admitted.
row_interpretation: replay rows, not unique independent windows; repeated CAL across nine models
CI_vs_native: All coverage/ADE/FDE/J estimates and intervals exactly [0,0] by identical outputs, not proof of equivalence of nontrivial methods.
limits: Joint geometry and stronger distribution-envelope rule does not isolate gate causality.
The envelope is stronger than original five pooled 1% gates; rejection does not mean an original gate necessarily fails.
Adaptive reuse of outputs, three seeds/scenes, overlapping windows, F16 seen pool and reused CAL; no independent generalization or pedestrian intent evidence.
Geometric nearness is not guaranteed same-candidate coverage redundancy.

DA2.issue: Zero lost and all motion PASS are vacuous gains under zero admission; report no coverage/ADE/FDE improvement.
DA2.counterargument: Current rule may reject useful physically acceptable complements; generation not disproved.

DA3.issue: Do not conclude fixed K20 integration is impossible or that any gate should be relaxed based on this exploratory null outcome.
DA3.next: Avoid deletion-rank or threshold sweeps; a new design should explicitly address safe admissible complementarity and native support. No automatic new model/loss/scorer.
